items.q: How do I generate my first animation?
items.a: Navigate to the Studio or Chat, enter a mathematical or scientific prompt (e.g. 'Explain the Fourier Transform with epicycles'), and click Generate. The agent pipeline will storyboard, synthesize Manim code, and render the scene.

items.q: Can I run AOS completely offline with local models?
items.a: Yes. AOS supports local Ollama models (such as Qwen 2.5 Coder and Llama 3.3) paired with Pocket TTS and local Docker Manim rendering for zero-cloud usage.

items.q: What video resolutions and framerates are supported?
items.a: AOS exports crisp 60 FPS vector animations in 1080p Full HD and 4K Ultra HD, as well as interactive HTML Manim Slides decks.

items.q: Why does the pipeline run a self-repair validation loop?
items.a: Generated Manim code passes through schema and AST validation before rendering. If syntax or runtime errors occur, the repair agent inspects traceback errors and recompiles automatically.

items.q: Can I inspect and edit the generated Manim code?
items.a: Yes. The complete lecture.py script and LectureIR JSON metadata are exposed in the UI and downloadable for custom fine-tuning or direct Manim CLI rendering.

items.q: What document formats are supported for syllabus ingestion?
items.a: PDF textbooks, Markdown lecture notes, Word documents (.docx), and LaTeX papers. EduClaw extracts core theorems, formulas, and structural headings.

items.q: How does EduClaw map textbook formulas to animations?
items.a: EduClaw vectorizes mathematical entities and maps definitions directly into SceneObject and Beat parameters so animations match authoritative textbook proofs.

items.q: How does Docker container rendering work?
items.a: Rendering occurs inside isolated manimcommunity/manim containers. Persistent container pools eliminate cold starts for fast scene compilation.

items.q: What is the difference between local and cloud GPU rendering?
items.a: Local rendering relies on your CPU or local GPU. Cloud GPU rendering provides high-throughput parallel rendering for long 4K lectures and multi-scene sequences.

items.q: How does Kyutai DSM synchronize narration with animation beats?
items.a: Delayed Streams Modeling (DSM) produces millisecond-accurate word-level timestamps that lock narration pauses and emphasis directly to visual animation cues.

items.q: What happens if audio synthesis is unavailable?
items.a: Narration synthesis is non-blocking. If audio service is disabled or fails, AOS automatically renders the full video without audio so rendering never stalls.
Yes. All Manim code execution runs inside isolated Docker containers without host filesystem access or network privileges.

items.q: Are prompts and uploaded textbooks used to train models?
items.a: Never. Prompts, documents, and generated video artifacts are strictly private and never used for public model training.

pillars.title: We don't train on your data

pillars.title: Vulnerability response
pillars.description: Patches for CVEs in dependencies merged within 72 hours. Coordinated disclosure for issues reported by researchers.

checklist: TLS 1.2+ on all traffic; HSTS preload
AES-256 encryption at rest for database and object storage
JWT short-lived access tokens (15 min) + httpOnly refresh tokens
API keys hashed in database; never logged or echoed
Per-org row-level scoping at the repository layer
Stripe handles all card data — we never see PAN/CVV
Incident postmortems published for any user-facing incident

items.a: AOS (Agentic Orchestration System) is an autonomous multi-agent platform that turns STEM concepts, mathematical formulas, and course notes into professional educational videos using Manim, Pydantic AI, and Kyutai Pocket TTS / DSM.

items.q: How does the generation pipeline work?
items.a: AOS runs an orchestrated Pydantic AI graph: Classify (audience & scope) → Plan (pedagogical outline) → Storyboard (scene breakdown) → Create Scenes (visual elements & LaTeX MathTex) → Add Beats (granular timings) → Add Narration → Validate & Repair (schema verification) → Synthesize Voice (Kyutai DSM) → Docker Render (60fps Manim compilation).

items.q: Can I run AOS locally with open-source models?
items.a: Yes! AOS natively supports local Ollama models (such as fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 Coder), offline resident Pocket TTS for narration, and local Docker Manim rendering without requiring external cloud APIs or paid tokens.

items.q: How does narration sync with animations?
items.a: Instead of blunt static pauses, AOS breaks each scene into visual beats and uses Kyutai Delayed Streams Modeling (DSM) to achieve millisecond-accurate word-level timestamps that align narration transitions exactly with visual elements.
You get 1080p and 4K MP4 videos, raw compilable Manim Community Python code (lecture.py), structured LectureIR JSON, and interactive presentation decks compatible with Manim Slides.

items.q: Can I edit and customize the generated animations?
items.a: Yes. Every visual object and beat is completely transparent. You can tweak parameters, edit the generated Python code, adjust timing beats, or re-render individual scenes directly in the web UI or CLI.

faqs.q: Can I run AOS completely offline for free?
faqs.a: Yes! AOS is open source. You can run local Ollama models (such as Qwen 2.5 Coder or Llama 3.3), local Pocket TTS, and local Docker Manim rendering completely free on your own machine.

faqs.q: What is included with Creator Pro?
faqs.a: Creator Pro includes dedicated cloud GPU nodes for rapid 1080p and 4K Manim rendering, Kyutai DSM streaming audio alignment, and EduClaw textbook ingestion.

faqs.q: What export formats does AOS produce?
faqs.a: Every generation outputs standard 60 FPS MP4 video files, raw compilable Manim Community Python code (lecture.py), LectureIR structured schemas, and interactive Manim Slides decks.

faqs.q: How does Kyutai speech synchronization work?
faqs.a: Delayed Streams Modeling (DSM) produces millisecond-accurate word-level timestamps that align visual beats and LaTeX formulas seamlessly with voiceover.

faqs.q: Can universities self-host on campus GPU clusters?
faqs.a: Yes. AOS is fully containerized and modular. You can deploy it using Docker Compose or Kubernetes on your on-premise compute infrastructure.

faqs.q: Do you offer academic or student discounts?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer special academic lab and campus-wide licensing with custom vector knowledge stores and priority GPU queues.
